Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Law 03/2016 restricts cross-border data transfers, requiring ANPDP authorisation or notification depending on whether the recipient jurisdiction provides adequate protection. The Leginon platform provides controlled institutional access to SIGA data via secure VPN. However, comprehensive data sharing rules for the forthcoming digital ID system are not yet published; the World Bank project targets a data strategy and action plan as an end-project deliverable. Scored 2 (Partially available).
revision_notes: Verified the two cited sources; the World Bank ID4D diagnostic PDF was only accessible as boilerplate front matter, but the dataprotection.africa fact sheet and the primary text of Law 03/2016 (Arts 19-24, sourced via afapdp.org) confirm cross-border data-transfer rules requiring ANPDP notification or authorisation. Cross-checked against São Tomé's National ICT agency (INIC) portal and its 2024 National Cybersecurity Strategy document, which confirm the National Interoperability Framework was published for public discussion in November 2021 but the accompanying Interoperability and Data-Sharing Law remains in draft (bill) form, not yet enacted. This corroborates the original assessment: general cross-border transfer rules are public, but comprehensive ID-system-specific data-sharing rules are not. Score of 2 (Partially available) confirmed.
revised_comments: Law 03/2016 (Personal Data Protection Law) publicly establishes procedural rules governing cross-border transfers of personal data, requiring notification to or prior authorisation from the National Data Protection Agency (ANPDP) depending on whether the recipient jurisdiction offers an adequate level of protection (Articles 19-24). A National Framework for Interoperability was published for public discussion in November 2021, but the accompanying Interoperability and Data-Sharing Law remains a draft bill, so comprehensive, ID-system-specific data-sharing rules have not yet been formally published. Institutional access to civil registry (SIGA) data is provided via the Leginon platform over a secure VPN with controlled access. Data-sharing rules are therefore only partially available.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 03/2016 (Personal Data Guarantee and Protection Law), enacted May 10, 2016, establishes a comprehensive data protection framework closely mirroring the EU Data Protection Directive (95/46/EC). It establishes the National Data Protection Agency (ANPDP), defines principles of lawfulness, transparency, proportionality and minimisation, and sets penalties for violations. Scored 2 (Yes).
revision_notes: Verified all three original sources plus the primary legal text of Law 03/2016 (via afapdp.org) and the RIPD (Ibero-American Data Protection Network) legislation registry entry. All corroborate that Law No. 03/2016, promulgated 10 May 2016, is a comprehensive data protection statute modelled on EU Directive 95/46/EC, covering lawful collection, processing, transfer and security of personal data, complemented by Law No. 07/2017 establishing the ANPDP. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed.
revised_comments: São Tomé and Príncipe has enacted comprehensive national data protection legislation: Law No. 03/2016 (Personal Data Protection Law), promulgated on 10 May 2016 and closely modelled on the EU Data Protection Directive (95/46/EC). It sets out principles of lawfulness, transparency, proportionality and data minimisation, establishes rules for the collection, processing, storage and cross-border transfer of personal data, and prescribes administrative penalties for non-compliance. The law applies to personal data processed by public and private bodies, including data linked to identity systems, and is complemented by Law No. 07/2017, which establishes the National Data Protection Agency (ANPDP) as the enforcement body.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The National Data Protection Agency (ANPDP - Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais) was established under Law 03/2016. It is operationally active, independently structured, empowered to investigate, subpoena evidence, impose fines, and publish annual reports. The Data Protection Africa fact sheet confirms the ANPDP is 'operational and relatively active in providing authorisations, resolutions, and opinions.' Scored 2 (Yes).
revision_notes: Verified both original sources plus fresher 2025 evidence of ongoing ANPDP activity: a January 2025 news report (rstp.st) quotes the ANPDP president describing active enforcement collaboration with Facebook to remove fake profiles impersonating public figures, and a forthcoming national AI ethics strategy; an August 2025 report from Portugal's data protection authority (CNPD) describes an institutional cooperation visit by an ANPDP board member under the Lusophone Data Protection Network. These confirm the ANPDP remains operationally active well beyond the original 2022 fact sheet citation. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed and strengthened.
revised_comments: The National Data Protection Agency (Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais, ANPDP), established under Law No. 07/2017, actively regulates the collection and sharing of personal data, including data linked to identity systems. As of 2025 the agency remains operationally active: it collaborates with Facebook to remove fraudulent profiles impersonating public figures, participates in the Lusophone Data Protection Network alongside the authorities of Portugal, Angola, Brazil and Cabo Verde, and is preparing a national strategy on the ethics of artificial intelligence. It is empowered to investigate complaints, issue authorisations and opinions, and impose administrative fines for non-compliance.
